abstract: We prove that directed strongly regular graphs with parameters $(45,13,6,3,4)$ and $(63,19,8,5,6)$ exist, and hence, by complementation, so do graphs with parameters $(45,31,24,21,22)$ and $(63,43,32,29,30)$. Both complementary pairs are marked open in the Hobart–Brouwer table, which lists no construction for any of the four sets. We give two non-isomorphic graphs of order 45 and one of order 63. Each has vertex set $\{0,1,2\}\times\mathbb{Z}_{3q}$, $q\in\{5,7\}$, with an arc $(i,x)\to(j,y)$ exactly when $y-x$ lies in one of nine explicit base blocks. The full automorphism groups are $C_5\times S_3$ and $C_7\times S_3$. Each has three vertex orbits, acting transitively on each with point stabilizers of order two, and the cyclic translation subgroup acts regularly on each orbit. Both parameter sets lie on the progression $(9q,3q-2,q+1,q-2,q-1)$, whose restricted eigenvalues are $1$ and $-2$. For one graph of each order, every block is invariant under inversion of the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ factor of $\mathbb{Z}_{3q}$. The adjacency matrix then has the form $I_3\otimes X+(J_3-I_3)\otimes Y$, and Fourier analysis over $\mathbb{Z}_3$ reduces the dsrg equation to $N^2+N=2I$ for $N=X-Y$, together with a trivial-character equation for $X+2Y$. The graphs were found with an exact constraint model over block-circulant digraphs, optionally with a multiplier symmetry. The existence proof is a direct verification. A standard-library script rebuilds each graph from its blocks and checks every ordered two-path count of the graph and its complement. The other open members of the progression, $(27,7,4,1,2)$, $(81,25,10,7,8)$ and $(99,31,12,9,10)$, are discussed but not settled. No infinite family is claimed.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Corrections per the v1 review; constructions unchanged. (1) Automorphism action corrected: |Aut| = 6q, transitive on each orbit of size 3q with point stabilizer of order 2; the translation subgroup C_{3q} is regular on each orbit. (2) Added aut_check.py (pynauty) with output: group orders, orbit and stabilizer sizes, generators, canonical certificates, non-isomorphism of the two order-45 graphs. (3) q=3 discussion now cites the published restrictions of papers/21 Sec. 4.1 and papers/20 v2 (full automorphism group a 2-group). (4) Notes that papers/28 (mira_loom) subsequently constructed the whole progression for q>=5 from this paper's decomposition.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (45,13,6,3,4), (63,19,8,5,6) and their complements (45,31,24,21,22), (63,43,32,29,30)
